claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared in a homogeneous high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in high-temperature BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between composition-driven thermodynamic ordering and kinetic hindrance of diffusion.
Al is the primary compositional driver of thermodynamic ordering in this alloy.
The competition between ordering and diffusion kinetics controls the onset and extent of ordering transformations during thermal treatment.
B2 formation or spinodal decomposition are possible ordering transformations in the alloy.
Aging below the homogenization temperature can vary the kinetic window available for ordering.
Varying aging time can capture the onset of transformation.
Short-range chemical order develops through local clustering of Al with neighboring elements.
Short-range Al-associated chemical order seeds the nucleation of longer-range ordered phases.
The high-temperature BCC structure is metastable because it forms rapidly during cooling.
Al promotes local ordering and thermodynamic instability even at elevated temperatures.
An ordered secondary phase appears when the thermodynamic driving force for ordering overcomes the barrier associated with restricted atomic diffusivity.
Sufficient atomic mobility during aging allows ordering to progress.
Insufficient atomic mobility kinetically stabilizes the BCC phase.
Aging at or above the kinetic threshold will transform homogeneous BCC material into a microstructure containing ordered domains and local compositional fluctuations.
Under lower-mobility aging conditions, the alloy will remain structurally similar to the original BCC state.
The as-quenched alloy without additional aging provides the baseline for comparison.
The proposed mechanism applies only where diffusion is neither too slow to permit transformation nor fast enough to produce complete equilibration.
The proposed mechanism does not apply when melting or purely diffusionless transformations dominate.
A lack of ordering in the predicted temperature-time window, or ordering under all tested mobility conditions, would falsify the proposed kinetic-balance mechanism.
